subject: tura
title: One macro tool (command_run) executes a stepped command graph per LLM turn: same-step reads run concurrently, mutating steps are barriers under shared/exclusive locks, later steps bind earlier step outputs
one_why: Collapses the inspect/patch/build/test/lint ReAct cycle into one model round trip; the corpus has no other harness that makes the tool surface one macro graph with an in-turn lock scheduler - clean-room port is an architecture decision, not a feature.

subject: tura
title: command_run steps execute speculatively against the still-streaming provider tool-call arguments, emitting streaming_partial updates and terminating the turn early (early_finish_reason) when a mid-graph apply_patch fails
one_why: Wall-clock win independent of tokens: the sandbox starts running the graph before the model finishes writing it, and a failed patch aborts the remaining model output rather than burning the turn.

subject: tura
title: Two-tier deterministic compaction with no summarizer LLM turn: agent-authored compact_context handoff from task_status, plus projection-based auto-compact; both rebuild a structured record with workspace snapshot, environment context, retained tool tail, and capability reset
evidence: crates/runtime/src/manas/process.rs:357-424 (handoff applied after persisted tool results), :442-458 and :1026-1047 (projected auto-compact, tested :1345-1375); crates/runtime/src/context/compaction.rs:101-150 (rebuild), :18 (max 2 inherited summaries)
one_why: Removes the extra summarizer round trip entirely and keeps execution state (commands, patches, validation evidence) as structured records instead of prose; the 2-generation cap on inherited summaries stops summary-of-summary drift.

subject: tura
title: task_status makes task state structured session data (task_group/status/task_type/compact_context) that mechanically drives prompt-manual selection, compaction handoff, and a startup gate: while task_type is unset, write-producing apply_patch steps are silently discarded from command_run before dispatch
one_why: Sequence policy enforced in the loop rather than asked of the model: no investigation state, no writes; distinct from validated-finish-gate, which gates the end, not the start.

subject: tura
title: TUI renders /approve <id> /deny <id> permission prompts and parses permission.asked/replied events, but no Rust code anywhere emits them; the gateway hardcodes allow:["*"] per agent and the runtime's permission layer always blocks requests it cannot route
evidence: apps/tui/src/tui/render.ts:133-138; apps/tui/src/gateway/events.ts:114-115; crates/runtime/src/tool_flow/permission.rs:8-33 (permission_denial_for_tool, request_command_run_sandbox_bypass always Err); crates/gateway/src/api/agent.rs:126-129 (PermissionRuleset allow vec!["*"] deny empty); grep permission.asked across crates: zero emitters
one_why: Users believe an approval gate exists; in fact TURA_APPROVAL_POLICY unset (the default) means no gating and there is no backend path that could ever ask - worse than absent, because the UI launders it.

subject: tura
title: Command interceptor is on by default and de-obfuscates before classifying (wrapper stripping, nested bash -c/eval recursion, connector chains, base64-to-shell, shell-variable alias following, workspace-aware deletion), but TURA_COMMAND_INTERCEPTOR_DISABLED=1 switches it off wholesale
one_why: Stronger default than nanocoder's opt-in jail, but a denylist plus a single env kill switch is still prompt-adjacent policy, not an enforced boundary; the workspace jail (--sandbox / TURA_COMMAND_RUN_SANDBOX) that does path-contain workdir and apply_patch (command_run/handler.rs:793; commands/apply_patch/mod.rs:307) is opt-in.

subject: tura
title: Guardrail tests prove effect, not classification: the interceptor e2e actually executes commands under a Docker POSIX harness and asserts the destructive side effect never happened, while safe commands must run for real (verified by their side effect)
one_why: Static blocked/allowed unit tables only test the classifier; end-to-end effect assertions test the whole wiring from model tool-call to process spawn - the gap where denylists usually fail.

subject: tura
title: Runtime leases make crash recovery a typed protocol: ActivateRuntimeLease with LeaseConflict/StaleLease outcomes, ReplayRuntimeRequest/RuntimeReplay journals, router startup orphan-worker reaping, and runtime-side parent watchdog
one_why: Two-process crash recovery where both sides can detect the other died (watchdog up, reaper down) and a spent runtime cannot revive itself via a stale lease - stronger resume semantics than any anchor except codex.

subject: tura
title: Loop e2e drives the full real pipeline - scripted codex-style SSE provider over a loopback TcpListener plus real tool execution in a temp workspace - and asserts final session state, tool results, and absence of stray tool calls
evidence: crates/runtime/tests/business/coding_agent_mock_e2e.rs:24-80; helpers/coding_agent_mock.rs:44,185 (mock bind), write_codex_sse :339+; CI runs per-crate: .github/workflows/ci.yml:95-149
one_why: Codex's mock-SSE suite pattern ported with real tools on the other side of the mock, giving loop-semantics tests without providers; the ceiling it shares with all anchors is that no model evals run in CI (caps verification at 8).

subject: tura
title: A CI job runs a Runtime Session equivalence gate against committed baselines with explicit failure-injection evidence artifacts uploaded each run
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:228-244 (Run Runtime Session equivalence gate; baseline.json, core-e2e.json, failure-injection.json uploads); tests/equivalence/runtime_session/ (runner, reference/, evidence json)
one_why: A refactor-grade behavioral contract that fails the build on drift and ships evidence - close to evals-in-CI in spirit without needing a model; exact gate semantics only partially verified from the runner scripts.

subject: tura
title: Cache discipline is append-only by construction: provider messages stored immutably per log record with stable per-result cache ids, and a stable per-session prompt_cache_key gated by provider support with four property tests
one_why: Compaction rewrites a record boundary rather than reshaping history, so provider-side prefixes stay cacheable across turns and across compaction; no cache warming (pi's edge) and coarse bytes/4 token estimates keep it below codex-9.

subject: tura
title: Internal process boundary is a documented anti-HTTP rule: gateway hosts the router, runtime workers are spawned subprocesses driven over a stdin/stdout JSON line envelope, and child-agent dispatch goes through the router CLI - never a URL - protected by contract crates
evidence: crates/runtime/src/manas/child_dispatch.rs:1-5 (binding rule comment: No internal URL communication may be introduced); crates/runtime/src/worker.rs:1-14 (line protocol envelope); Cargo.toml:26-31 (router_contract, runtime_contract, session_log_contract)
one_why: Removes localhost-port attack surface and makes orphan/process recovery the OS's job (reap + watchdog) instead of a reconnect protocol; contract crates keep the wire types honest across the workspace.
